messages:
Anya: quick sync — finalizing request/response schema conventions for chat/completions/embeddings. main open items: token usage field names, placement of trace/request ids, metadata surface (model+version+caller), and launch criteria for the API change. proposed: prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / total_tokens, top-level trace_id + request_id, and a small meta object for model/version. thoughts?

Michael: +1 on a single convention across endpoints. prefer snake_case. small nit: use input_tokens / output_tokens instead of prompt_/completion_ — clearer for embeddings. also +1 to top-level request_id/trace_id for easier ingestion into logs.

Jessica: concern about breaking changes for SDKs — current clients expect usage.tokens or similar. we need a migration strategy and feature flag. must include: (1) dual-name support for 2 releases, (2) docs + SDK PRs, (3) changelog callout in console.

Samir: privacy reminder: do NOT include full prompt or any PII in metadata. include only a prompt_hash or prompt_id if we need to tie back. add a retention TTL on telemetry objects. also for embeddings where tokenization is fuzzy, return token_count as optional or token_estimate to avoid confusion.

Anya: good points. let's vote on naming: A) prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens (matches many APIs) B) input_tokens/output_tokens/total_tokens (more explicit for embeddings). if majority prefers B, we go with that and provide mapping helpers in SDKs.

Michael: vote B. also recommend adding field names to use for billing: billing_input_tokens and billing_output_tokens (internal only) so customers see the simpler names but billing maps to exact internal counters.

Jessica: vote B. i'll own the SDK compat plan: dual field ingestion + adapter that normalizes to the new names. will draft migration notes and examples.

Samir: abstain on naming but +1 to token_estimate for embeddings. will draft the retention policy and PII checklist.

Anya: sounds good. agreement: use input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens as public schema. include optional token_estimate for embeddings if exact tokenization not computed. top-level request_id and trace_id will be required in responses. meta will include model and model_version only. sensitive fields (raw prompt/user_message) must never be included in metadata.

Anya: example response sketch (for docs):
```json
{
  "request_id": "r_01F...",
  "trace_id": "trace-2026-03-...",
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "model_version": "2026-03-12",
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 34,
    "output_tokens": 120,
    "total_tokens": 154
  },
  "token_estimate": null,          // used for embeddings when we can't guarantee exact token counts
  "response": {
    "choices": [ { "text": "..." } ]
  }
}
```

Michael: nice. for trace_id format propose: <region>-<instance>-<unixsec>-<short-rand> so ops can correlate to infra. share a generator helper in the runtime.

Jessica: launch criteria proposal: 1) spec doc updated and merged, 2) SDK adapters released (py/js/go), 3) migration guide published, 4) telemetry for both old and new fields for min 2 weeks, 5) console changelog notice & beta flag for existing tenants.

Samir: add compliance step: data retention policy updated + internal runbook for redact requests. also ensure KMS keys used for prompt hashes if stored.

Anya: agreed. let's scope for next sprint but break into sub-tasks. owners: Michael -> API spec + runtime trace generator (#1423), Jessica -> SDK migration + docs, Samir -> retention & compliance, Anya -> product signoff + rollout schedule. I'll create the umbrella ticket and link sub-issues. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Deployment notice — created ticket REDWOOD-1423 and linked to repo redwood/docs.

Anya: thanks all — will post the spec PR link here once created. if anyone has last concerns post them in thread, otherwise i'll close and move to implementation. :wave:
